title: GitHub Issues 101 — Labels, Milestones, and Assignees
learning_objectives: Explain what GitHub Issues are and how they fit into a development workflow
Understand the purpose of labels, milestones, and assignees
Configure standard labels for a personal project (bug, feature, docs, etc.)
Create a milestone to group related issues by goal or timeframe
outline: What GitHub Issues are: the connective tissue between ideas and code
Anatomy of an issue: title, body, labels, milestone, assignee, comments
Labels: categorizing by type (bug, feature, docs) and priority (high, low)
Default GitHub labels vs. custom label sets for personal projects
Milestones: grouping issues into goals or releases
Assignees: relevant even for solo projects (self-accountability)
Hands-on: Configure Helm's label set and create the first milestone (MVP v1)

helm_context.deliverable: Helm label set configured and MVP v1 milestone created

criteria: At least 6 labels configured (covering type and priority)
MVP v1 milestone created with a target date
Can explain what each label and milestone represents in the context of Helm

professor_constraints: Keep this high-level and practical — no deep dives into GitHub API or automation
Use Helm MVP features to motivate the label/milestone setup (task management, calendar sync, etc.)
Suggest a lean label set appropriate for a solo project — don't over-engineer
